# webarchiver

> Current documentation index generated from the exact MkDocs navigation.
> Capability and content-use claims are operator-scoped and provenance-bound.

## Home

- [Home](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/) — Webarchiver API + MCP Server built on the connector SDK — a typed connector with one read-only tool per operation.

## Overview

- [Overview](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/overview/) — > Category: Integration | Ecosystem Role: MCP Server > Built on scion-sdk.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/architecture/) — The webarchiver package owns external-system operations and source mappings. The shared connector SDK owns reusable runtime contracts.

## Installation

- [Installation](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/installation/) — webarchiver is a standard Python package and a prebuilt container image.

## Deployment

- [Deployment](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/deployment/) — This page covers documentation delivery and running webarchiver as long-lived servers.

## Usage (API / CLI / MCP)

- [Usage (API / CLI / MCP)](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/usage/) — webarchiver exposes the same capability three ways: as MCP tools an agent calls, as a Python API you import, and as a CLI.

## Backing Platform (Webarchiver)

- [Backing Platform (Webarchiver)](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/platform/) — webarchiver is a client of a backing service instance. This page provides a Docker recipe for deploying one locally as an operator-selected provider endpoint.

## Glossary

- [Glossary](https://knuckles-team.github.io/webarchiver/glossary/) — The browser operator experience for working with agents and their runtime. Arbora hosts it as a composed service.
